summary: We are testing whether an enhanced MaxRects packer with four specific improvements (contact-point heuristic, bin transposition, pairwise-swap local search on item orderings, and 6-strategy randomized search) can exceed the iteration-1 baseline score of 88.78, with a target of 93+. One experiment arm will implement the full algorithm in solution.cpp and measure the judge score across 15 hidden test cases.
key_points: Iteration 1 achieved 88.78 using basic MaxRects + Skyline with density-weighted random ordering; this iteration adds four mechanisms to reduce packing fragmentation: contact-point placement scoring, bin transposition (packing in H×W then translating coordinates), local search via pairwise type-order swaps, and an expanded set of 4 placement methods (BSSF, BAF, BL, CP).

The single arm runs 96 deterministic packing configurations (4 methods × 6 orderings × 2 rotation choices × 2 bin orientations), then a pairwise-swap local search phase (~250ms budget), then randomized ordering exploration (~830ms budget), all within the 1-second time limit per test case.

Confirmation: judge score ≥ 93 (≥5-point improvement over 88.78). Refutation: score ≤ 89 would indicate the new mechanisms don't help or introduce regressions. Key risk is TLE on large inputs — if the 96 deterministic runs plus local search exceed 1s, some test cases will score 0, which should be diagnosable from a score drop well below 88.

Parameters are conservative: free-rect cap at 500 prevents quadratic blowup, time budgets leave ~170ms margin, and the algorithm falls back to the best deterministic solution if random search finds nothing better.

Design is sound for approval: the mechanisms are independent and additive, the code changes are confined to solution.cpp, and the measurement command is a single judge invocation that reports a 0–100 score.
